'''Pamela Gail Coxson''' is an American applied mathematician specialized in [[Disease models|disease modelling]]. She is retired as a specialist in the division of general and internal medicine at the [[University of California, San Francisco]] Center for Vulnerable Populations. 

== Life ==
Coxson completed a Ph.D. in mathematics from [[University of Southern California]]. Her 1979 dissertation was titled ''On the equivalence between open loop and closed loop control laws for linear systems''. Alan Schumitzky was her doctoral advisor.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|8944}}</ref>

In 1985, while working as a fellow at the [[Mary Ingraham Bunting Institute]], Coxson initiated the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]]' Sonia Kovalevsky Math Day program for female high schoolers and their teachers.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Morrow |first=Charlene |url= |title=Notable Women in Mathematics: A Biographical Dictionary |last2=Perl |first2=Teri |date=1998 |publisher=[[Greenwood Publishing Group]] |isbn=978-0-313-29131-9 |language=en |author-link2=Teri Perl|page=213}}</ref> In 1986, Coxson was a visiting assistant professor of mathematics at [[Ohio State University]]. One of her mentors was [[Violet B. Haas]], whom she met in 1983.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Case |first=Bettye Anne |url= |title=[[Complexities: Women in Mathematics]] |last2=Leggett |first2=Anne M. |date=2016 |publisher=[[Princeton University Press]] |isbn=978-0-691-17109-8 |language=en|author-link=Bettye Anne Case| author-link2=Anne M. Leggett|page=205}}</ref>

Coxson has worked in several areas of [[applied mathematics]] including  mathematics in [[pharmacokinetics]], [[catalytic cracking]] of oil, satellite image processing, and [[medical imaging]].<ref>{{Cite book|page=75|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->  |title=Applying Modeling to Improve Health and Economic Policy Decisions in the Americas The Case of Noncommunicable Diseases: The Case of Noncommunicable Diseases |date=2015 |publisher=[[OECD Publishing]] |isbn=978-92-64-24360-6 |language=en}}</ref> Formerly working as a specialist in the division of general and internal medicine at the [[University of California, San Francisco]] Center for Vulnerable Populations,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cvp-sf.com/staff.php|title=Staff|work=UCSF Center for Vulnerable Populations|access-date=2025-04-24}}</ref> she retired in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://epibiostat.ucsf.edu/sites/g/files/tkssra2066/f/DEB_newsletter_July_2018.html|date=July 2018|title=Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics Newsletter|publisher=UCSF Department of Epidemiology and Biostatistics|access-date=2025-04-24}}</ref>
